label: One being whose esse is its essence is a first cause of being of every other actual being
paraphrase: Some n in act as to being, whose represented esse equals its essence, has no actual cause of its esse (no c with ActualEsseCause c n), and every other being x in act as to being descends from n through a finite chain of actual causes of being (Relation.TransGen of ActualEsseCause; mode of causing unspecified, tenseless). 'First cause' means exactly this: uncaused in that order and at the head of a chain to each other actual being. It is De ente c.3 [69874]'s 'aliqua res, quae sit causa essendi omnibus rebus, eo quod ipsa est esse tantum', read as first cause in the chain rather than direct cause. Not asserted: direct causation of every esse, present conservation, efficient causation, necessary existence, concreteness at a world, uniqueness among necessary beings, or God identification.
